currentContext.business: Phoenix Overseas Limited operates three disclosed business verticals. The Merchant Export Division trades and markets animal feed products and agricultural commodities (corn/maize, oil cakes, spices, food grains, pulses, soybean meal, de-oiled rice bran) sourced from third-party suppliers, exports primarily to Bangladesh and other Asian markets on a bulk B2B model, and also undertakes bulk imports of lentils such as urad dal and tur dal for domestic demand. The Fashion Accessories Division manufactures and exports jute, cotton, canvas, PP and leather bags plus belts, wallets, purses and other leather goods from Sodepur, Kolkata to Europe, the UAE and Australia, serving international retail chains including Woolworths Group, Australia. The Cold Storage Division runs a multipurpose cold storage (including a dedicated potato unit) at Malda, West Bengal providing storage, handling and distribution for perishables, and has introduced controlled-atmosphere mushroom cultivation; during FY2025-26 the Company additionally entered the industrial gloves segment.

Fashion Accessories Division: bags for men and women in jute, cotton, canvas and leather
Cold Storage Division: storage/handling/distribution for fruits (apples, oranges), vegetables (carrots, potatoes, chili, ginger), dairy and frozen products (ice cream, sweets), seafood (fish), eggs and other allied goods

risks.risk: Single-market concentration on Bangladesh, exposed by prolonged political turmoil
risks.note: Management states FY2025-26 was 'one of the most challenging years for the Company's operations due to heightened geopolitical uncertainties across the globe, particularly the disruptions in Bangladesh, which adversely affected international trade and business activities.' The Chairman adds that Bangladesh 'has been our largest market for decades' and that during the turmoil 'Orders slowed, payments stretched' [Chairman quote back-filled from the sibling profile / strategy_outlook / capex_expansion bundles - the Chairman's message was not routed into this risks bundle]. This is a demand-side AND a receivables-collection risk concentrated in one sovereign, and it is the single largest structural exposure the AR discloses. Management states the situation has since stabilised.

'The Company's operations were also impacted by significant volatility in foreign exchange rates ... which affected procurement costs, pricing strategies and overall trade margins.' As an importer of lentils and an exporter of commodities and manufactured goods, the Company carries two-way FX exposure. The routed text discloses no hedging policy, no hedged proportion and no forex risk-management framework.

risks.risk: Global commodity price volatility passing straight through a thin-margin trading model
risks.note: 'fluctuations in global commodity prices, which affected procurement costs, pricing strategies and overall trade margins.' The Merchant Export Division's products 'are primarily procured from third-party suppliers' - the Company is a merchant intermediary, not a producer, so it owns neither the input cost base nor the output price and absorbs the spread compression directly. The MD&A itself notes profitability moderated even as turnover hit a five-year high.

risks.risk: Revenue concentration in one of three segments
risks.note: The MD&A states 'the Merchant Export Division remaining the key driver of revenue growth, while the Fashion Accessories and Cold Storage Divisions continued to provide stable and recurring income.' The diversification narrative therefore rests on two divisions that are small relative to the trading business; the new industrial gloves vertical is at entry stage. (Segment revenue and segment-result figures are printed in the routed text but are a segment P&L and are deliberately NOT extracted.)

risks.risk: Geopolitical dependence of the new-market strategy (Middle East)
risks.note: The Middle East and South-East Asia entries 'are expected to generate meaningful business opportunities once geopolitical conditions, particularly the ongoing conflict in the Middle East, stabilise.' By management's own framing, the payoff from this year's principal geographic diversification is conditional on an external event outside the Company's control and with no stated timeline.

'As on March 31, 2026, the Company had 19 employees, including its Directors' - a nineteen-person organisation running a merchant export business of five-year-record turnover across three (now four) verticals and multiple export geographies. Management explicitly attributes the year's navigation to 'the extensive experience of the management team in international trade', which concentrates institutional knowledge in a handful of people. Succession relevance: the MD's re-appointment is being put to shareholders for a further 5 years from 21 July 2026.

risks.risk: Related-party density: sales to, and guarantees for, companies with common directors
risks.note: Board's Report item 34 asserts all RPTs were at arm's length, in the ordinary course, under Audit Committee omnibus approval, and that none is 'material' under revised Regulation 23 of the SEBI Listing Regulations. However Form AOC-2 [PROVENANCE: sibling governance_entities bundle] shows the Company giving guarantees in respect of loans availed by BCL Bio Energy Private Limited (also a 29% associate) and by BCPL Railway Infrastructure Limited, and booking Sales to Resilient Strategic Advisors Private Limited (also a 33.83% associate) - i.e. off-balance-sheet credit support to, and revenue from, entities that are simultaneously associates and common-director parties. Amounts deliberately not extracted; the structural entanglement, not the size, is the risk.

risks.risk: An undisclosed secretarial-audit exception, and a mid-cycle statutory auditor change
risks.note: Board's Report item 29 reads 'Except as stated below, there are no qualifications, reservations, adverse remarks and disclaimers of the Secretarial Auditors in their Secretarial Audit Report for the Financial Year 2025-26' - and NOTHING follows; the exception itself is not delivered in any of the six bundles, while item 27 separately claims the Secretarial Audit Report 'does not contain any qualification, reservation or adverse remark'. The two statements contradict each other and the substance is unread. Separately, the 23rd AGM notice seeks to appoint M/s. L.B. Jha & Co. LLP as Statutory Auditor to fill a CASUAL VACANCY caused by M/s. Jain Seth & Co. [PROVENANCE: sibling governance_entities bundle], with no reason for the departure stated anywhere in the routed text.

risks.risk: Policy-driven import substitution in the pulses the Company imports
risks.note: The MD&A itself highlights the 'Mission for Aatmanirbharta in Pulses: A six-year, Rs 11,440 crore mission targeting self-reliance in Tur, Urad, and Masoor ... guarantees 100% procurement at Minimum Support Prices'. The Company's Merchant Export Division 'undertakes bulk imports of lentils, including urad dal and tur dal, to meet domestic demand' [second clause back-filled from the Corporate Overview in this bundle], so the same government programme the AR presents as sector tailwind is directed at the demand the Company's import book serves. The AR does not itself flag this as a risk.
